issues.legal_issue: An adoption is established where credible evidence proves the giving and taking of the child, supported by a deed executed at the time of the adoption.
material_facts: The adoptive widow and several witnesses described the adoption ceremony and the giving and taking of the child.
The witnesses’ evidence was accepted as credible, and the scribe explained his presence at the ceremony.
A deed of adoption was executed on the same day as the ceremony and registered later.
The adoptive widow testified to the adoption even though it divested her of her interest in the property.
issues.conclusion: The Court upheld the finding that the adoption had in fact taken place.
issues.legal_principle: Giving and taking is the essence of adoption. Credible testimony describing that ceremony can establish the adoption, and a deed executed contemporaneously with the adoption provides supporting evidence.

predicates.adoption_status_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning whether an adoption took place.
predicates.witnesses_described_giving_and_taking: The adoptive parent and other witnesses described the child being given and taken in the adoption ceremony.
predicates.contemporaneous_adoption_deed: A deed recording the adoption was executed at the time of the ceremony.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerning an adoption includes witness descriptions of giving and taking and a deed executed at the ceremony, the adoption fact is established.

issues.legal_issue: A widow is presumed to have authority to adopt to her deceased husband unless an express prohibition by him is established.
material_facts: The widow made the adoption long after her husband’s death, when she had been in her twenties at his death.
The adoption deed did not state that she had authority from her husband, and her earlier pleading in a partition or maintenance suit did not mention authority to adopt.
No express prohibition by the husband was established; the circumstances relied on by the opposing parties did not reasonably establish one.
The widow’s delay was explained by her concern that an adoption would divest her of property, and later legislation gave a deceased coparcener’s widow an interest in family property.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the widow was presumed to have authority to adopt and that the circumstances relied on did not rebut that presumption.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9(1) of the Mysore Hindu Law Women’s Rights Act, 1933, presumes, in the absence of an express prohibition in writing, that a widow has authority to adopt to her husband. The presumption may be rebutted by direct or circumstantial evidence establishing an express prohibition. The delay was explicable, the existence of daughters did not establish prohibition, and omission of authority from the deed or an earlier pleading was irrelevant because the law did not require the widow to announce her authority. Section 8 of the Act gave a deceased coparcener’s widow a right to share in family property.

rule.if: adoption_authority_dispute and widow_made_adoption and no_express_prohibition_established and (adoption_was_delayed or husband_left_daughters or adoption_deed_omitted_authority or earlier_pleading_omitted_authority)

predicates.adoption_authority_dispute: The proceeding disputes whether a widow had authority to adopt to her deceased husband.
predicates.widow_made_adoption: A widow made an adoption to her deceased husband.
predicates.no_express_prohibition_established: The evidence does not establish that the husband expressly prohibited his widow from adopting.
predicates.adoption_was_delayed: The widow made the adoption a substantial time after her husband’s death.
predicates.husband_left_daughters: The deceased husband left one or more daughters.
predicates.adoption_deed_omitted_authority: The deed recording the adoption did not state that the husband had authorized it.
predicates.earlier_pleading_omitted_authority: An earlier pleading by the widow did not mention authority to adopt.

issues.definition: When authority to adopt is disputed, no express prohibition is established, and one or more of the listed circumstances is present, the widow is presumed authorized to adopt.
